text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Religious leaders have a key role in ensuring Singaporeans of different faith continue living side by side in peace, Minister for Community Development Abdullah Tarmugi says.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton, more popular than ever according to poll, takes oath of office for second time, and hopes to usher in a new season of cooperation.
- Newly appointed Education Minister Teo Chee Hean says he will study education system very carefully to see how to realise Singaporeans' potential more fully.
- Fifty-two construction workers died in 1996, making construction industry the one with highest number of fatal accidents.
- Singapore Telecom eyes more "Belgacom-type" deals in Asia-Pacific region as part of new overseas investment strategy.
- China's central bank will be forced to intervene to prevent Chinese currency from appreciating this year and to keep country on track to achieve economic targets.

- Self-made businessman Joseph Gondobintoro plans to make GMG Holdings, newly formed company, regional flagship for his global businesses after it completes proposed takeover of ElectroMagnetic (1992) Ltd.
- Newly available figures show average monthly subsales of new apartments fell by two thirds after property curbs introduced by government last May.

- All not lost for Singapore's money brokers, now hurting from effects of electronic deal matching systems, as profits could resume more healthy course as Asia's financial markets grow in sophistication and depth.
- Malaysian property developer Sateras Resources Bhd says it expects bulk of future profits to come from property and cement ventures in China and locally.
- Hing Yiap Knittting Industries Bhd's offer of 2.001 million shares available to Malaysian public oversubscribed 191 times.
